title: No Aadhaar? NRI Students Can Apply for JEE Main 2027 With Passport
excerpt: The NTA says NRI applicants without Aadhaar, PAN or an Indian driving licence can enter passport details instead — fresh applications without a late fee close November 22, 2026.
body:
• NRI students without Aadhaar, PAN or an Indian driving licence can complete the JEE Main 2027 application using a valid passport, the National Testing Agency (NTA) has clarified.
  • Act by November 22, 2026 to file a fresh Session 1 application without a late fee; applications with a late fee run November 23 to 26, and the correction window is November 27 to 29, 2026.
  • Your name, parents' names and date of birth in the form must match your passport and your Class 10 certificate exactly.
  • Help: NTA helplines 011-40759000 and 011-69227700, email jeemain@nta.ac.in; apply on the official portal, jeemain.nta.nic.in.

NRI students who do not hold Aadhaar, a PAN card or an Indian driving licence can apply for JEE Main 2027 using a valid passport, the National Testing Agency (NTA) has clarified. The clarification, reported by Jagran Josh, answers registration problems that overseas applicants ran into during Session 1 registration.

Responding to a student query about authentication barriers in the online process, the agency said: "You can use a passport to complete the application process." Passport details can be entered directly in the designated identification fields on the website, rather than relying only on a domestic identity document.

Who is affected, exactly

The clarification is aimed at Non-Resident Indian and other overseas applicants for JEE Main 2027 Session 1 who lack an active domestic identity card. This year's registration runs through MeriPehchan, the National Single Sign-On facility: candidates sign in through DigiLocker, JanParichay or e-Pramaan, and the system fetches identity details from that account, as explained by Careers360. That design is where NRI applicants without Aadhaar-linked records were getting stuck at the authentication and e-KYC stages. The passport route gives those candidates a way to complete the form.

What changed, precisely

The NTA pointed candidates to two recent notices. A public notice on October 28, 2026 set out the registration guidelines, including logging in through DigiLocker, JanParichay or e-Pramaan and completing re-KYC through DigiLocker. A second notice on October 30, 2026 allowed candidates who had already applied, generated an application number or paid the fee to submit a fresh application form instead; a new application number is issued for the fresh form. The key practical point for NRI candidates is that a passport is now an accepted proof of identity for completing the application when Aadhaar, PAN or a driving licence is not available.

Dates that matter

Fresh applications without a late fee can be submitted until November 22, 2026. Fresh applications with a late fee run from November 23 to 26, 2026 — Careers360 put the Session 1 late fee at Rs 500. Candidates who only need to fix details, including identification parameters, can use the correction window from November 27 to 29, 2026. One cost warning: examination fees paid on an earlier application will neither be refunded nor adjusted against a fresh application, so a candidate who files again should expect to pay the fee again.

What to do next

Apply on the official website, jeemain.nta.nic.in. Enter your passport details carefully and check them before submitting: the name, parents' names and date of birth in the registration form must match your passport records and your Class 10 board certificate exactly, and the name and date of birth must also match the Class 10 certificate or marksheet under the October 28 guidelines. Overseas candidates should also choose their test city early: the NTA conducts JEE Main in overseas centres including Dubai, Sharjah, Doha, Muscat, Riyadh, Kuwait City, Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, and those centres fill up quickly. Fees for centres outside India are higher than domestic centres, so make sure an international card is enabled for cross-border transactions before paying. For technical problems with passport entry or upload, contact the NTA on 011-40759000 or 011-69227700, or email jeemain@nta.ac.in. A date-by-date summary is also available from Disha Stars.

For diaspora families, the clarification removes a documentation barrier that had nothing to do with eligibility: a student living abroad can now register on the strength of the passport they actually hold, provided the details are consistent across the passport, the form and the Class 10 record.
